players.product: High-purity nano-grade BaTiO3 (barium titanate) dielectric powder

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2027 (April - June 2026) results, Director and Executive Officer (IR) on the call: net sales rose 6.6% year on year as the strong Electronic Materials business, driven by continuing robust AI-server demand, and other businesses covered the loss of sales from ending the titanium dioxide business; operating income fell 10.5% on lower titanium dioxide volumes and the pull-back in pharmaceutical API intermediates (organic chemicals) whose sales were concentrated in the prior-year first quarter; net income attributable to owners of parent JPY 20 hundred million, up 56%, on a gain on the planned sale of a fixed asset (a disposal site).
quarterly_data.figure: net sales +6.6%; operating income -10.5%; net income attributable to owners of parent JPY 20 hundred million (+56%)

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance (call): the first-half and full-year FY2027 plans are kept at the figures announced on May 13. AI-server demand in the Electronic Materials business is expected to stay strong, but the company will watch demand trends from the second quarter onward.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 and FY2027 plans unchanged from May 13

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2027 segments (call): Electronic Materials sales and profit rose on strong AI-server demand and steady automotive demand. Cosmetic Materials: sales up, profit down (weak domestic sales, overseas recovery, higher costs from ending titanium dioxide). Organic Chemicals: sales and profit down (API intermediates shipments concentrated in the prior-year Q1). Hygiene Materials, Contract Processing, Catalysts and Inorganic Materials: sales and profit up. Titanium Oxide and Zinc Products: sales and profit down on the end of pigment-grade titanium dioxide. Resin Additives: sales up, profit down (Thailand's weak economy). Medical: sales up, profit down (raw-material costs for ethical drugs, an Alloid G price cut).

Management (call Q&A) on AI-server demand for Electronic Materials: customers have identified almost none of its products to the company as being for AI servers, but by the company's own estimate some part numbers have grown very strongly over the past year or two - in the last fiscal year some part numbers roughly doubled (about 2 times) year on year, which the company presumes are for AI servers. Those part numbers are still growing steadily, though not at a 2x pace, and management expects the momentum to continue. The growth is concentrated in its high-end, differentiated, higher-margin products.
quarterly_data.figure: some part numbers about 2x year on year last fiscal year (company's estimate of AI-server use)

quarterly_data.signal: Management (call Q&A) on capacity for these Electronic Materials products: capacity is becoming quite full, and capital investment to expand it is being considered quite concretely.
quarterly_data.figure: capacity nearly full; expansion capex under concrete study

quarterly_data.signal: Management (call Q&A) on the Middle East situation (Strait of Hormuz): this fiscal year's price revisions were basically made in response to the resulting rise in raw-material prices, and so-called price corrections had little impact this time, for all segments; the cost increase from higher raw-material prices is being covered by passing prices on to customers. Procurement has so far avoided any situation where materials run out and production stops, and management does not see that risk at present.
